mainTopic: Leftovers of a מנחה and of animal offerings, and whether a קומץ needs a כלי שרת
overview: The amud opens by finishing a challenge against רב שילא. A ברייתא seems to say that impure blood sprinkled on purpose is not accepted, but the גמרא reads 'on purpose' as describing how the blood became impure. A new משנה teaches that if the שיריים of a מנחה become impure, burned, or lost, the offering is valid by רבי אליעזר and invalid by רבי יהושע. רב limits this to a case where all the שיריים are ruined. The גמרא concludes that a remainder counts (שיורא מילתא היא), and supports this with רבי יהושע's rule that a כזית of meat or fat is enough to sprinkle the blood. It then learns from ״חֵלֶב״ and ״לְרֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ״ that any part of the animal burned on the מזבח counts, but the accompanying מנחה does not. A second משנה discusses a קומץ that was not handled with a כלי שרת, where רבי שמעון is lenient. The גמרא explains his view, defends רבי יהודה בריה דרבי חייא and רב נחמן בר יצחק against several ברייתות, and begins a new ברייתא that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A ברייתא seems to contradict רב שילא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: impure blood sprinkled by mistake is accepted, but sprinkled on purpose is not. This seems to go against רב שילא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: Blood that became impure and was sprinkled — by mistake, it is accepted; on purpose, it is not accepted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge רב שילא, who said the ציץ makes impure blood acceptable even when it is sprinkled on purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא seems to separate mistake from purpose when it comes to the sprinkling. If sprinkling on purpose is not accepted, then רב שילא's claim that it is accepted looks wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: By mistake, without knowing
On purpose, knowingly
It was accepted (the offering works and brings atonement)
Sprinkling the blood on the altar

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Blood that became impure and he sprinkled it
if by mistake — it is accepted;
if on purpose — it is not accepted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of רב שילא's view.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב שילא's ruling that the ציץ makes impure blood acceptable even when sprinkled on purpose
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא appears to say sprinkling on purpose is not accepted, which goes straight against רב שילא.

steps.title: Mistake or purpose refers to how it became impure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the ברייתא: the mistake or purpose is about how the blood became impure, not about the sprinkling.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: Blood that became impure and was sprinkled, whether by mistake or on purpose — if it became impure by mistake, it is accepted; if on purpose, it is not accepted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב שילא by explaining that the ברייתא is talking about how the blood became impure, not how it was sprinkled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the new reading, the sprinkling can be by mistake or on purpose and it does not matter. What matters is whether the blood became impure by mistake (accepted) or on purpose (not accepted). Now the ברייתא fits רב שילא.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means (rereading a source)
Whether... or...

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב שילא, the important question is how the blood became impure, not whether the sprinkling was on purpose.
steps.confusionAlert: The words שוגג and מזיד show up twice. In the second part they describe how the blood became impure, not the sprinkling.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
Blood that became impure and he sprinkled it,
whether by mistake or on purpose —
if it became impure by mistake, it is accepted;
if on purpose, it is not accepted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 1.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Mistake or purpose referred to the act of sprinkling.
steps.terutzMaskana: Mistake or purpose refers to how the blood became impure; sprinkling on purpose can still be accepted.

steps.title: משנה: Leftovers of a מנחה become impure, burned, or lost
steps.stepSummary: If the שיריים of a מנחה become impure, burned, or lost, the offering is valid by רבי אליעזר's principle and invalid by רבי יהושע's principle.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If its leftovers became impure, were burned, or were lost — by רבי אליעזר's principle it is valid, and by רבי יהושע's principle it is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה rules on a מנחה whose leftover portion (the part the כהנים eat) can no longer be eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה applies an argument about animal offerings to a מנחה. רבי אליעזר holds the blood may be sprinkled even with no meat to eat, so the קומץ may be burned without edible שיריים. רבי יהושע needs something edible, so here the מנחה is invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
The leftover part of the מנחה, after the קומץ is taken, eaten by the כהנים
Principle or approach
Valid / invalid
The handful of the מנחה burned on the altar

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the topic for the rest of the סוגיא: does the קומץ still work when the שיריים are gone or impure?

phrases.english: MISHNA:
If its leftovers became impure,
its leftovers were burned, or its leftovers were lost —
by the principle of Rabbi Eliezer, it is valid,
phrases.notes: This is his view about animal offerings, that blood may be sprinkled even when there is no meat left to eat.

phrases.english: and by the principle of Rabbi Yehoshua, it is invalid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה; a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the שיריים can't be eaten: valid by רבי אליעזר, invalid by רבי יהושע.

steps.title: רב: Only when all the leftovers became impure
steps.stepSummary: רב says the משנה's invalid ruling applies only when all the שיריים became impure, not just part of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב said: This is only when all of its leftovers became impure, but if only some of its leftovers did, then no.
steps.whatsHappening: רב narrows the משנה: by רבי יהושע, the מנחה is invalid only if all the leftovers became impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If even part of the שיריים is still pure, the קומץ may be burned and the מנחה stays valid. This adds a limit the משנה did not say.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is only when (a limiting phrase)
All
Part, some

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Rav said:
And this is only when all of its leftovers became impure,
but if only part of its leftovers — not.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: וְהוּא שֶׁנִּטְמְאוּ כׇּל שְׁיָרֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the משנה's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מנחה is invalid only when all the שיריים became impure; if only part did, it stays valid.

steps.title: Assumption: רב helps only for impure, not for lost or burned
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא assumes רב's leniency for partial שיריים applies only to impurity, not to loss or burning.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think: if part became impure — yes, it is valid; but if part was lost or burned — no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next question by noticing that רב spoke only about impurity. It assumes that loss or burning of part would still make the מנחה invalid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רב mentioned only נטמא, it seems that for partial loss or burning he did not say the מנחה stays valid. That difference needs a reason, and the next steps look for one.

keyTerms.meaning: You might think (a starting assumption)
Lost
Burned
Yes

phrases.english: It enters your mind:
if part became impure — yes, it is valid;
if part was lost or burned — no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from רב's wording.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Working assumption: רב's leniency covers only partial impurity, not partial loss or burning.

steps.title: What is רב's reasoning?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what idea leads רב to separate impurity from loss and burning.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does he hold?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what reasoning stands behind רב's ruling. This sets up two possible answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question opens a two-sided test. Each possible reasoning will be checked against רב's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: What does he hold? (what is his reasoning)

phrases.english: What does he hold?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the assumption in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reasoning that would let רב treat partial impurity differently from partial loss or burning.

steps.title: If leftovers count, lost or burned should work too
steps.stepSummary: If רב holds that a partial leftover counts, then partial loss or burning should also leave the מנחה valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he holds that a remainder is significant — then even if part was lost or burned, too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first option: maybe רב holds that whatever is left is enough. That would also cover loss and burning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a remaining piece of שיריים is enough to justify burning the קומץ, it should not matter how the rest was ruined. So this reasoning cannot explain why only impurity helps.

keyTerms.meaning: A remainder, what is left over
It is significant, it counts

phrases.english: If he holds that a remainder is significant —
then even if part was lost or burned, also!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First side of the question in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that רב helps only for partial impurity
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a remainder counts, then loss and burning of part should be valid too, so the distinction falls.

steps.title: If leftovers don't count and the ציץ helps, all impure should work too
steps.stepSummary: If a remainder does not count and partial impurity is fixed by the ציץ, then the ציץ should fix even fully impure שיריים.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he holds a remainder is not significant, then why does impure work? Because the ציץ makes it acceptable? If so, even all of its leftovers too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the second option: a remainder doesn't count, and impurity is helped only by the ציץ. But then the ציץ should help even when all the leftovers are impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ציץ fixes impurity no matter how much became impure. So with this reasoning, רב's limit to 'only part' makes no sense. Both options fail, and the next step resolves this.

keyTerms.meaning: The golden plate on the כהן גדול's forehead that makes impure offerings acceptable
Makes acceptable
It is not significant, it doesn't count
If so

steps.whatToRemember: Both possible reasons fail: if a remainder counts, loss and burning should work too; if the ציץ is the reason, even fully impure leftovers should work.
steps.confusionAlert: The middle line, 'what is the reason it works when impure? Because the ציץ makes it acceptable', is the גמרא explaining the second option for itself before attacking it. It is not a separate ruling.

phrases.aramaic: אִי קָסָבַר: שִׁיּוּרָא לָאו מִילְּתָא הִיא,
phrases.english: If he holds that a remainder is not significant,
then when impure, what is the reason? Because the frontplate makes it acceptable?
If so, then even all of its leftovers too!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי קָסָבַר: שִׁיּוּרָא לָאו מִילְּתָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second side of the question in step 6, after the first side failed in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's limit that only partial impurity keeps the מנחה valid
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the ציץ is what fixes impurity, it should work for all the שיריים, not just part, so רב's limit to 'only part' falls apart.

steps.title: רב really holds a remainder counts, even for loss and burning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא retracts its earlier assumption. רב holds שיורא מילתא היא, so partial loss or burning is also valid. He mentioned impurity only because the משנה lists it first.
steps.simpleTranslation: Actually, רב holds that a remainder counts. 'Became impure' includes lost and burned too. He said 'became impure' only because that is the first case listed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the two challenges by saying its assumption about רב was wrong. רב's leniency covers impurity, loss and burning equally.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 5-8 assumed רב separated impurity from loss and burning, which made his view hard to explain. Now the גמרא says there is no difference: since a remainder counts, any partial loss leaves the מנחה valid. The word נטמא was just a shorthand taken from the first case in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually / really; drops an earlier assumption
A remainder counts as something significant
And the same law applies
He mentioned the first of the cases

steps.whatToRemember: רב holds שיורא מילתא היא. If part of the שיריים is impure, lost or burned, the rest saves the מנחה.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רב treats impurity as special. He only named impurity because it is the first case in the משנה.

phrases.english: Actually, he holds:
a remainder is something significant,
and 'became impure' — the same applies to lost and burned,
and the fact that he said 'became impure'
is because he took the first of them.
phrases.notes: The משנה lists impure first, then burned and lost, so רב just used the first word.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenges of steps 7-8 by dropping the assumption from step 5
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the earlier assumption and reads the wording as shorthand
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's leniency applies only to impurity, not to loss or burning
steps.terutzMaskana: רב holds a remainder counts in all three cases; נטמא just echoes the first case in the משנה

steps.title: רבי יהושע: an olive-bulk left from an offering allows sprinkling the blood
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports the idea that a remainder counts. If a כזית of meat or fat is left from an offering, the blood is still sprinkled.
steps.simpleTranslation: As taught in a ברייתא: רבי יהושע says, for any offering in the Torah where a כזית of meat or a כזית of fat remains, the כהן sprinkles the blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that matches the view that a remainder counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The meat and fat of an offering relate to its blood the way the שיריים of a מנחה relate to its קומץ. רבי יהושע rules that even a small leftover, as little as a כזית, is enough to allow the blood to be sprinkled. So a remainder counts.

keyTerms.meaning: An olive-bulk, the minimum amount that counts
Animal offerings
Fats burned on the מזבח
Sprinkles the blood on the מזבח

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא:
Rabbi Yehoshua says:
All the offerings in the Torah
from which there remained
an olive-bulk of meat or an olive-bulk of fat
he sprinkles the blood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source that matches the view of step 9
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of רבי יהושע: a remaining כזית of meat or fat allows sprinkling the blood

steps.title: Half-olive-bulks, the burnt offering, and the meal offering
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא goes on. Half a כזית of meat and half a כזית of fat do not combine. In an עולה they do combine, because it is all burned. A surviving מנחה does not allow sprinkling.
steps.simpleTranslation: If half a כזית of meat and half a כזית of fat remain, he does not sprinkle. In an עולה, even then he sprinkles, since it is all burned. With a מנחה, even if it is fully intact, he does not sprinkle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the same ברייתא of רבי יהושע. It now gives the limits of the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Meat is eaten and fat is burned, so their halves do not join into one כזית. In an עולה both are burned on the מזבח, so the halves join. The last line says a remaining מנחה cannot save the blood, which sets up the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: Half an olive-bulk
Burnt offering, fully burned on the מזבח
Entirely consumed by fire
Still intact / still exists

steps.confusionAlert: Two halves combine only when both parts go to the same place. In an עולה everything goes on the מזבח.

phrases.aramaic: כַּחֲצִי זַיִת בָּשָׂר וְכַחֲצִי זַיִת חֵלֶב –
phrases.english: Half an olive-bulk of meat and half an olive-bulk of fat
he does not sprinkle the blood,
and with a burnt offering, even

phrases.aramaic: כַּחֲצִי זַיִת בָּשָׂר וְכַחֲצִי זַיִת חֵלֶב –
phrases.english: half an olive-bulk of meat and half an olive-bulk of fat
he sprinkles the blood,
because it is entirely burned,
and with a meal offering, even if all of it remains,
he shall not sprinkle.

steps.triggerLanguage: כַּחֲצִי זַיִת בָּשָׂר וְכַחֲצִי זַיִת חֵלֶב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with its limits
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Halves of meat and fat combine only in an עולה. A surviving מנחה does not allow the blood to be sprinkled.

steps.title: Why does the ברייתא mention a meal offering?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what a מנחה has to do with sprinkling blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: A מנחה — what is it doing here?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is puzzled by the last line of the ברייתא and sets up an explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מנחה is flour and has no blood. Why would anyone think a מנחה could be a reason to sprinkle blood? The גמרא needs to know which מנחה the ברייתא means.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it doing here / what is its connection?

phrases.english: A meal offering — what is it doing here?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the last ruling of the ברייתא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which מנחה is meant, and how it relates to sprinkling blood

steps.title: רב פפא: it is the meal offering that accompanies the animal
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the ברייתא means the מנחת נסכים. You might think it counts as part of the animal offering, so the ברייתא teaches that it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: it is the מנחת נסכים. You might have thought that since it comes with the offering, it is like the offering itself. The ברייתא teaches us that it is not.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the question. He names the מנחה and explains why the ברייתא had to mention it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מנחת נסכים is brought together with an animal offering. One might think that if the meat became impure but this מנחה survived, it could count as the offering's remainder. The ברייתא rules that out: only the animal's own meat or fat can save the blood.

keyTerms.meaning: Meal offering brought along with the wine libations of an animal offering
You might have thought
Together with
It teaches us (otherwise)

steps.whatToRemember: Only a כזית of the animal's own meat or fat lets the blood be sprinkled. The מנחת נסכים that comes with it does not count.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
It is the meal offering of the libations.
It could enter your mind
that since it comes together with an animal offering,
it is like the body of the offering itself,
so it teaches us that it is not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The מנחה is the מנחת נסכים. The ברייתא teaches that it is not treated as part of the animal for sprinkling the blood.

steps.title: Where does this rule come from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the ברייתא's rule that the blood is sprinkled even if only a כזית of fat remains.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא from step 10 and asks for its source in the Torah. This short question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said the blood may be sprinkled even if only fat is left and no meat. The גמרא now wants a פסוק that teaches this.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these words (rules) learned? A request for a source.

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?
phrases.notes: He means the rule from the ברייתא: if a כזית of fat is left, the blood is still sprinkled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ברייתא from step 10 and asks for its verse source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source for sprinkling the blood when only fat remains and no meat.

steps.title: The verse mentions only fat, not meat
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, quoting רבי ישמעאל (and some say רבי יהושע בן חנניה), brings the פסוק ״וְהִקְטִיר הַחֵלֶב לְרֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ לַה׳״. It mentions only fat, so fat alone is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי ישמעאל, and some traced it back to רבי יהושע בן חנניה: The verse says "And he shall burn the fat for a pleasing aroma to ה׳." Fat alone is enough, even if there is no meat.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer is a פסוק about sprinkling blood that speaks only about burning the fat. From this we learn that fat is enough, even without meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same פסוק that talks about sprinkling the blood mentions only the fat being burned. It says nothing about meat. So the sprinkling still works when only fat survived and the meat is gone.

keyTerms.meaning: And they traced it to. Some carried this teaching back to an earlier sage.
And he shall burn (on the מזבח)
The fats of an animal offering that are burned on the מזבח

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Yishmael,

phrases.aramaic: וּמָטוּ בַּהּ מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן חֲנַנְיָא:
phrases.english: and some traced it to Rabbi Yehoshua ben Chananya:
The verse says: "And he shall burn the fat
for a pleasing aroma to ה׳."

phrases.aramaic: חֵלֶב – וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין בָּשָׂר.
phrases.english: Fat: even if there is no meat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק ״וְהִקְטִיר הַחֵלֶב לְרֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ״ mentions only fat, so the blood may be sprinkled even when no meat remains.

steps.title: What about the liver lobe and the kidneys?
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק covers fat. The גמרא asks how we know the blood is sprinkled if only the lobe of the liver or the two kidneys remain.
steps.simpleTranslation: We found a source for fat. From where do we know the same about the lobe of the liver and the two kidneys?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the source for fat. Now it asks about other parts that also go on the מזבח: the יותרת and the two kidneys.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says ״חֵלֶב״, which seems to cover only fat. The liver lobe and the kidneys are also burned on the מזבח, but they are not called fat. So the גמרא needs a separate source for them.

keyTerms.meaning: And we have found (a source for one case)
The lobe of the liver, which is burned on the מזבח
The two kidneys, also burned on the מזבח
From where do we know it?

phrases.english: And we have found a source for fat;
the lobe of the liver and the two kidneys, from where do we know?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַשְׁכְּחַן חֵלֶב, יוֹתֶרֶת וּשְׁתֵּי כְּלָיוֹת מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the source for fat and asks about other parts burned on the מזבח.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether, and from where, the blood is sprinkled when only the liver lobe or kidneys remain.

steps.title: The ברייתא's mention of a מנחה implies the kidneys count
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says only that a מנחה does not allow sprinkling. This implies that the liver lobe and kidneys do allow it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: "And with a מנחה, even if all of it remains, he does not sprinkle." It is a מנחה that does not allow sprinkling. But the lobe of the liver and the two kidneys do allow it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers from the end of the ברייתא (step 11). The ברייתא excluded only the מנחה. So other parts of the animal, like the liver lobe and the kidneys, must still count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא chose to exclude only the מנחה that comes with the offering. If the liver lobe and kidneys were also excluded, it should have said so. Its silence shows that they count, because they are part of the animal.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught (in the ברייתא)
Remains, still exists (here: remains pure)
He shall sprinkle (the blood on the מזבח)
But this. Introduces an inference: what the text implies about a different case.

phrases.english: As it is taught: "And with a meal offering,
phrases.notes: This is the end of the ברייתא from step 11. By step 13 it was explained as the מנחת נסכים that comes with the animal.

phrases.english: even if all of it remains, he does not sprinkle."
It is a meal offering for which he does not sprinkle;
but for the lobe of the liver and the two kidneys, he sprinkles.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּקָתָנֵי: וּבַמִּנְחָה, אֲפִילּוּ כּוּלָּהּ קַיֶּימֶת לֹא יִזְרוֹק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 16 by drawing an inference from the ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because the ברייתא excludes only the מנחה, the liver lobe and kidneys do allow the blood to be sprinkled.

steps.title: The verse source: ״לְרֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ״
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the verse behind the ברייתא's rule about the kidneys. רבי יוחנן himself learns it from ״לְרֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ״: anything you offer up as a pleasing aroma counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this? רבי יוחנן himself said: "For a pleasing aroma" means anything that you offer up for a pleasing aroma.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tells us that the kidneys count, but the גמרא wants to know which פסוק teaches it. רבי יוחנן answers from the words ״לְרֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ״ in the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words ״לְרֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ״ are read broadly. Any part of the animal that goes up on the מזבח as a pleasing aroma is enough to allow the sprinkling. That includes the liver lobe and the kidneys, not only the fat.

keyTerms.meaning: His own (רבי יוחנן's own teaching, not one he quoted from someone else)
A pleasing aroma. The Torah's description of parts burned on the מזבח.
Offer up (on the מזבח)

phrases.english: From where do we know this?
Rabbi Yochanan himself said:

phrases.aramaic: ״לְרֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ״ – כֹּל שֶׁאַתָּה מַעֲלֶה לְרֵיחַ נִיחוֹחַ.
phrases.english: "For a pleasing aroma": anything that you offer up for a pleasing aroma.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks for a פסוק behind the inference of step 17 and finds it.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״לְרֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ″ includes everything offered on the מזבח, such as the liver lobe and kidneys.

steps.title: Why the verse needs both ״חֵלֶב״ and ״לְרֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ״
steps.stepSummary: Both words are needed. ״חֵלֶב״ alone would leave out the kidneys, and ״לְרֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ״ alone would include even the מנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was necessary to write "fat," and it was necessary to write "for a pleasing aroma." If the Torah had written only "fat," I would say: fat, yes; the lobe of the liver and the two kidneys, no. So the Torah wrote "pleasing aroma." And if the Torah had written only "for a pleasing aroma," I would say it includes even a מנחה. So the Torah wrote "fat."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why both words in the פסוק are needed. Each one fixes a mistake we would make if we had only the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״לְרֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ״ widens the rule beyond fat to the liver lobe and the kidneys. ״חֵלֶב״ limits the rule to parts of the animal itself, so the מנחת נסכים that comes with it does not count. Together they give exactly the ברייתא's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: It was necessary (for the Torah to write it)
I would have said. What we would wrongly think without this word.
The Merciful One. A name for ה׳ as the One who gave the Torah.
Yes / no

steps.whatToRemember: The blood is sprinkled if any part of the animal that goes on the מזבח remains (fat, liver lobe, kidneys). ״לְרֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ״ teaches this, and ״חֵלֶב״ shows that the accompanying מנחה does not count.

phrases.english: And it was necessary to write "fat,"
and it was necessary to write "for a pleasing aroma."

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִי כְּתַב ״חֵלֶב״ הֲוָה אָמֵינָא: חֵלֶב – אִין,
phrases.english: For if it had written only "fat," I would say: fat, yes;
the lobe of the liver and the two kidneys, no.
So the Merciful One wrote "pleasing aroma."
And if the Merciful One had written only "for a pleasing aroma,"
I would say: even a meal offering counts.
phrases.notes: This is the מנחת נסכים that comes along with the animal, as in step 13.

phrases.english: So the Merciful One wrote "fat."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that two words of the פסוק have been used, the גמרא explains why each one is needed.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: ״לְרֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ״ includes all parts of the animal burned on the מזבח, and ״חֵלֶב״ excludes the accompanying מנחה. Together they produce the ברייתא's rule.

steps.title: New משנה: a handful not handled with a service vessel
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a קומץ not handled with a כלי שרת is פסול, but רבי שמעון says it is כשר. A קומץ burned in two parts is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: MISHNA: If the handful was not in a service vessel, it is unfit, and רבי שמעון says it is fit. If he burned its handful in two parts, it is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It brings a מחלוקת about a קומץ that was not handled with a כלי שרת, and adds that burning the קומץ in two parts is fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא holds that the קומץ must go through a כלי שרת, so without one it is פסול. רבי שמעון disagrees and calls it כשר. The second ruling teaches that the קומץ does not need to go on the fire all at once.

keyTerms.meaning: A holy service vessel used in the בית המקדש
The handful taken from a מנחה and burned on the מזבח
Rules it valid (fit)
Twice, here meaning in two parts

phrases.english: MISHNA:
If it was not in a service vessel, it is unfit,
phrases.notes: "It" is the קומץ, the handful taken from the מנחה.

phrases.english: and רבי שמעון deems it fit.
If he burned its handful twice, it is fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ שֶׁלֹּא בִּכְלֵי שָׁרֵת – פָּסוּל, וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מַכְשִׁיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the earlier discussion about fat and blood ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A קומץ not handled with a כלי שרת is פסול according to the תנא קמא and כשר according to רבי שמעון. Burning the קומץ in two parts is כשר.

steps.title: What is רבי שמעון's reason?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בריה דרבי חייא asks for the source behind רבי שמעון's lenient ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: רבי יהודה, son of רבי חייא, said: What is the reason of רבי שמעון?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks why רבי שמעון allows a קומץ without a כלי שרת. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא's view is easy to understand, since normally holy service needs a כלי שרת. רבי שמעון's lenient view needs a source, so the question focuses on him.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: GEMARA:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא:
phrases.english: רבי יהודה, son of רבי חייא, said:
What is the reason of רבי שמעון?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of רבי שמעון's view in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק or reasoning behind רבי שמעון's ruling that the קומץ is כשר without a כלי שרת.

steps.title: Like a sin offering or like a guilt offering
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק compares a מנחה to both a חטאת and an אשם. By hand, like a חטאת, it must be the right hand. With a vessel, like an אשם, even the left hand works.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: "It is most holy, like the sin offering and like the guilt offering." If he comes to do it by hand, like a חטאת, he must do it with the right hand, like a חטאת. If with a vessel, he may do it with the left hand, like an אשם.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה בריה דרבי חייא answers his own question with a פסוק. It shows two allowed ways to bring the קומץ: by hand or in a vessel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק gives the מנחה two models, so there are two valid ways to offer it. If the כהן copies the חטאת and uses his hand, he must use the right hand. If he copies the אשם and uses a vessel, the left hand is also allowed. This is why רבי שמעון does not require a כלי שרת.

keyTerms.meaning: Most holy, the highest level of קרבנות
Sin offering
Guilt offering
The right hand
The left hand

steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון is not saying 'anything goes.' In this explanation there are two set ways: by hand with the right hand only, or with a vessel, where the left hand is also fine.

phrases.english: The verse says:
"It is most holy, like the sin offering and like the guilt offering."
If he comes to do its service by hand, like a sin offering,
he does it with the right hand, like a sin offering.
If with a vessel, he may do it with the left hand, like a guilt offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא ״קֹדֶשׁ קָדָשִׁים הִיא כַּחַטָּאת וְכָאָשָׁם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question by giving a פסוק as רבי שמעון's source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because the מנחה is compared to both a חטאת and an אשם, it may be offered by hand (right hand only) or with a vessel (even the left hand).

steps.title: רבי ינאי: once taken from a service vessel, any way works
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי reads רבי שמעון as more lenient: after the קומץ is taken from a כלי שרת, it may be brought up even in a belt or a clay pot.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי ינאי said: Once he took the handful from a service vessel, he may bring it up and burn it even in his belt, and even in a clay pot.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ינאי gives a different explanation of רבי שמעון. In his view, once the קומץ has been taken from a כלי שרת, the way it is carried to the מזבח does not matter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה בריה דרבי חייא allowed only two set ways. רבי ינאי allows any way at all, even ordinary objects like a belt or a clay pot. The one requirement he keeps is that the קומץ was first taken from a כלי שרת.

keyTerms.meaning: A belt or sash
A clay pot, an ordinary non-holy vessel
He brings it up to the מזבח and burns it

phrases.english: And רבי ינאי said:
Once he took the handful from a service vessel,
he may bring it up and burn it even in his belt,
and even in a clay pot.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יַנַּאי אָמַר: כֵּיוָן שֶׁקְּמָצוֹ מִכְּלֵי שָׁרֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a broader reading of רבי שמעון than the one in the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון, once the קומץ was taken from a כלי שרת, it may be brought up and burned in any way, even in a belt or a clay pot.

steps.title: Everyone agrees the handful needs sanctification
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says all agree that the קומץ needs קידוש in a כלי שרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: All agree that the handful needs sanctification.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק adds a point both sides agree on: the קומץ must be sanctified in a כלי שרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows the limit of the מחלוקת. Even רבי שמעון does not drop the קידוש of the קומץ. The argument is only about how the קומץ is brought up and burned.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
Making it holy by placing it in a כלי שרת
Requires

steps.whyThisMatters: This marks exactly what רבי שמעון is lenient about: carrying and burning the קומץ, not its קידוש.

phrases.english: רב נחמן בר יצחק said:
All agree about the handful that it requires sanctification.
phrases.notes: "All" includes רבי שמעון, so even he requires this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the מחלוקת by stating what both sides agree on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone, including רבי שמעון, agrees that the קומץ requires קידוש in a כלי שרת.

steps.title: A ברייתא allows even the left hand by hand
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the קומץ, the קטורת, and the לבונה are כשר whether brought up by hand or in a vessel, with the right hand or the left. This seems to refute רבי יהודה בריה דרבי חייא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They objected: The burning of fats, limbs, and wood that he brought up, whether by hand or with a vessel, whether with the right hand or the left, they are fit. The handful, the incense, and the frankincense that he brought up, whether by hand or with a vessel, whether with the right hand or the left, they are fit. This is a refutation of רבי יהודה son of רבי חייא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that allows the קומץ to be brought up by hand even with the left hand. It calls this a תיובתא against רבי יהודה בריה דרבי חייא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה בריה דרבי חייא said that by hand, the קומץ must be offered with the right hand, like a חטאת. The ברייתא allows by hand with the left hand too. So his explanation seems to clash directly with this source.

keyTerms.meaning: The limbs of an animal קרבן
The incense
Frankincense, burned with a מנחה
A strong refutation

steps.confusionAlert: The refutation is only against רבי יהודה בריה דרבי חייא, who required the right hand when done by hand. It does not attack רבי ינאי, who allows any way.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
The burning of fats, limbs, and wood that he brought up,
whether by hand or with a vessel,
whether with the right or with the left, they are fit;
the handful, the incense, and the frankincense that he brought up,
whether by hand or with a vessel,
whether with the right or with the left, they are fit.

phrases.aramaic: תְּיוּבְתָּא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא!
phrases.english: This is a refutation of רבי יהודה son of רבי חייא!
phrases.notes: He said in step 22 that by hand, only the right hand is allowed.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: הֶקְטֵר חֲלָבִים וְאֵבָרִים וְעֵצִים שֶׁהֶעֱלָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רבי יהודה בריה דרבי חייא's explanation in step 22 and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה בריה דרבי חייא's rule that a קומץ brought by hand must be offered with the right hand.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says a קומץ is כשר by hand even with the left hand, which directly contradicts his requirement of the right hand.

steps.title: The ברייתא lists separate cases
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בריה דרבי חייא reads the ברייתא as separate cases: by hand it must be the right hand, but with a vessel either hand works.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה בריה דרבי חייא could answer you: the ברייתא is teaching separate cases. By hand, it must be the right hand. With a vessel, it can be either the right or the left.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 25 by rereading the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא seemed to say that either hand works in every case. Now we read 'right or left' as going only with 'in a vessel,' while 'by hand' requires the right hand. That matches exactly what רבי יהודה בריה דרבי חייא learned from the פסוק in step 22.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches separate cases; each part of the list goes with a different situation
Right hand
Left hand

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָךְ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda, son of Rabbi Chiya, could say to you:
It teaches separate cases:
by hand, with the right hand;
with a vessel, whether with the right or with the left.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא: לִצְדָדִין קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 25
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the ברייתא as separate cases (לצדדין)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא allows the left hand even when bringing up by hand
steps.terutzMaskana: The left hand is allowed only with a vessel; by hand, only the right hand works

steps.title: A ברייתא where רבי שמעון allows any vessel
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון accept the קומץ if it was put in any vessel. This seems to contradict רב נחמן בר יצחק.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if the כהן took the קומץ not from a כלי שרת, sanctified it not in a כלי שרת, and brought it up and burned it not in a כלי שרת, it is פסול. רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון say it is כשר if it was placed in a vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now attacks רב נחמן בר יצחק from step 24, who said everyone agrees the קומץ needs קידוש in a כלי שרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this ברייתא, רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון accept the קומץ when it was placed in a vessel, even though no כלי שרת was used. If any vessel is good enough, then רבי שמעון does not require קידוש in a כלי שרת. That breaks רב נחמן בר יצחק's 'all agree.'

keyTerms.meaning: A holy vessel used in the בית המקדש service
Took a handful (the קומץ) from the מנחה
Sanctified the קומץ by placing it in a כלי שרת
Burned it on the מזבח
They rule it valid
Placing it into a vessel

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע: קְמָצוֹ שֶׁלֹּא מִכְּלֵי שָׁרֵת,
phrases.english: Come and hear: If he took the handful not from a service vessel,
and sanctified it not in a service vessel,

phrases.aramaic: וְהֶעֱלוֹ וְהִקְטִירוֹ שֶׁלֹּא בִּכְלִי שָׁרֵת – פָּסוּל,
phrases.english: and brought it up and burned it not in a service vessel, it is unfit.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מַכְשִׁירִין בְּמַתַּן כְּלִי.
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon rule it fit when it was placed in a vessel.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: קְמָצוֹ שֶׁלֹּא מִכְּלֵי שָׁרֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from defending רבי יהודה בריה דרבי חייא to challenging רב נחמן בר יצחק
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן בר יצחק's claim (step 24) that all agree the קומץ needs קידוש in a כלי שרת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון accepts the קומץ placed in any vessel, so he does not require קידוש in a כלי שרת

steps.title: Read it as: from the כלי שרת onward
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads רבי שמעון's leniency as starting only after the קומץ was placed in a כלי שרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say: from the placing in the vessel and onward.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by changing how we understand 'במתן כלי.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון are not saying any vessel works. They mean that once the קומץ was placed in a כלי שרת and sanctified, it no longer needs a כלי שרת for the rest of the process. So קידוש in a כלי שרת is still needed, just as רב נחמן בר יצחק said.

keyTerms.meaning: Say instead; read the words this way
And onward, from that point on

phrases.english: Say: from the placing in a vessel and onward.
phrases.notes: He means that once the קומץ was placed in a כלי שרת, the later steps don't need one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 27
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Placing the קומץ in any vessel is enough for רבי שמעון
steps.terutzMaskana: A כלי שרת is needed for קידוש; after that, no כלי שרת is required
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as saying no כלי שרת is needed at all. The leniency only starts after the קומץ has already been placed in a כלי שרת.

steps.title: רבי שמעון needs only the קמיצה from a כלי שרת
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that for רבי שמעון, once the קומץ is taken from a כלי שרת, it can be brought up and burned without one. He does not mention קידוש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: The חכמים say the קומץ requires a כלי שרת. How? He takes it from a כלי שרת, sanctifies it in a כלי שרת, and brings it up and burns it in a כלי שרת. רבי שמעון says: once he has taken it from a כלי שרת, he may bring it up and burn it without a כלי שרת, and that is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא to challenge רב נחמן בר יצחק again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים list three stages that need a כלי שרת: taking the קומץ, קידוש, and bringing it up. רבי שמעון says that after the קומץ is taken from a כלי שרת, 'that is enough,' and he skips קידוש. This suggests he does not require קידוש in a כלי שרת, against רב נחמן בר יצחק's 'all agree.'

keyTerms.meaning: Requires
How so?
Brings it up to the מזבח
It is enough for it

phrases.english: Come and hear: And the Rabbis say:
The handful requires a service vessel. How?

phrases.aramaic: קוֹמְצוֹ מִכְּלִי שָׁרֵת, וּמְקַדְּשׁוֹ בִּכְלִי שָׁרֵת,
phrases.english: He takes the handful from a service vessel, and sanctifies it in a service vessel,
and brings it up and burns it in a service vessel.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: כֵּיוָן שֶׁקְּמָצוֹ מִכְּלִי שָׁרֵת,
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: Once he has taken the handful from a service vessel,

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲלוֹ וּמַקְטִירוֹ שֶׁלֹּא בִּכְלִי שָׁרֵת וְדַיּוֹ.
phrases.english: he brings it up and burns it not in a service vessel, and that is enough.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: קוֹמֶץ טָעוּן כְּלִי שָׁרֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to רב נחמן בר יצחק after the first was answered
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן בר יצחק's claim (step 24) that all agree the קומץ needs קידוש in a כלי שרת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון makes only the קמיצה from a כלי שרת necessary and says 'דיו', which implies no קידוש in a כלי שרת is needed

steps.title: Reading the ברייתא as requiring sanctification first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the ברייתא from step 29. רבי שמעון means that once the כהן removed the קומץ and sanctified it in a כלי שרת, he may bring it up and burn it without a vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say it this way: once he took the handful and sanctified it in a service vessel, he brings it up and burns it, and that is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 29 by adding one word to the ברייתא: קידוש, meaning sanctifying the קומץ in a כלי שרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 29 was a problem because the ברייתא said nothing about putting the קומץ into a כלי שרת. The גמרא says to read it as "he took it and sanctified it in a כלי שרת." So the vessel is still needed for קידוש, as רב נחמן בר יצחק holds. רבי שמעון's leniency only applies to bringing it up and burning it afterward.

keyTerms.meaning: "Say": read the source this way. It is used to reinterpret a text.
He sanctified it, by placing the קומץ into a כלי שרת.
A sacred service vessel of the מקדש.
He brings it up to the מזבח and burns it.
It is enough for it; nothing more is needed.

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי שמעון (as the גמרא reads him), the קומץ must still be sanctified in a כלי שרת. Only the later stages, bringing it up and burning, can be done without one.

phrases.english: Say:
once he removed the handful and sanctified it in a service vessel,
phrases.notes: The words "and sanctified it" are what the גמרא is adding to the ברייתא from step 29.

phrases.english: he brings it up and burns it, and that is enough for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא: כֵּיוָן שֶׁקְּמָצוֹ וְקִדְּשׁוֹ בִּכְלִי שָׁרֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the קשיא of step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the ברייתא: adding the missing stage of קידוש in a כלי שרת.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say רבי שמעון needs no כלי שרת at all once the קומץ was taken.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא means that after the קומץ was sanctified in a כלי שרת, no vessel is needed for bringing it up and burning it.

steps.title: A new ברייתא about moving the קומץ from right hand to left
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a new source. If the כהן took the קומץ with his right hand and put it into his left, he must return it to his right. The ברייתא then starts a second case, about a קומץ in his left hand, which continues in the next section.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if he took the handful with his right hand and put it in his left, he should return it to his right. In his left...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new attempted proof from a ברייתא. Here it only begins quoting the source, and the point it wants to make comes in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first case teaches that a קומץ which ended up in the left hand is not lost. The כהן simply moves it back to the right hand and continues. The word בשמאלו opens a second case, and the full source and its use in the debate will appear once the quote is finished.

keyTerms.meaning: He removed a handful (the קומץ) from the מנחה.
Right hand / left hand. עבודה is normally done with the right hand.
He should return it, moving it back to its proper place.

steps.confusionAlert: The quote is cut off here. Do not decide yet whom this ברייתא challenges or supports; the rest comes in the next section.

phrases.english: Come and hear: if he removed the handful with his right hand
and put it in his left hand,
he should return it to his right hand.
If it was in his left hand...
